title: AWS Backup Restore Job Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.39 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.39 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:events` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="Backup Job State Change" (detail.state="FAILED" OR detail.state="ABORTED")
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.39_aws_backup_restore_job_f_39"
| sort -_time
description: Restore job failures prevent recovery during DR. Monitoring ensures backup and restore pipeline is healthy.
value: Detecting aws backup restore job failures early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Create EventBridge rule for Backup Job State Change. Filter for FAILED/ABORTED. Optionally ingest backup job list from AWS Backup API for compliance dashboard. Run periodic restore tests and log results.
visualization: Table (job, resource, state, message), Timeline (failed restores), Single value (failed jobs last 24h).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where (match(All_Changes.app, "(?i)backup|aws.?backup") OR match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)backup.*job"))
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.status span=1d
| sort -count

Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. knownFalsePositives: Jobs that you cancelled on purpose, DR drills, and pre-prod runs that you expect to fail a gate.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:events`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `detail-type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Create EventBridge rule for Backup Job State Change. Filter for FAILED/ABORTED. Optionally ingest backup job list from AWS Backup API for compliance dashboard. Run periodic restore tests and log results.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="Backup Job State Change" (detail.state="FAILED" OR detail.state="ABORTED")
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.39_aws_backup_restore_job_f_39"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:events` in `index=aws` to detect aws backup restore job failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `detail-type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_39_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (job, resource, state, message), Timeline (failed restores), Single value (failed jobs last 24h)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aws backup restore job failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
